chapter_theme: The middle states within waking (மத்திய சாக்கிர அவத்தை): waking itself holds all five states, each tied to a mala or power, and the tattvas are counted differently by each school (96, 36, 28, 24 and 25). The soul in the sakala state gropes like a blind man, but by grace and Nandi's teaching it learns that it is the knower beyond the inert tattvas, sheds states, malas and tattvas, and stands as one.
structure_note: The states within waking and their powers (2167 to 2170); grace beyond the tattvas (2171); counts of the tattvas and the yogic body (2172 to 2178), with the schools' counts set side by side (2179); the knower and release from tattvas and malas (2180 to 2182); the malas graded by the rank of beings (2183).

2167.reading: Within waking, waking-of-waking belongs to the concealing power, waking-dream to Mahamaya, the pressing stage of waking to one's karma, and waking-turiya to maya.
2167.nuance: திரோதாயி (the concealing power), மாமாயை, காமியம் (karma) and மாயை are four of the five malas or bonds; the verse names four sub-states. அழுத்தி is obscure, perhaps for deep sleep (சுழுத்தி) within waking.

2168.reading: Maya rouses kala and the tattvas after it, among them raga; passing through turiya, deep sleep, dream and waking, the soul comes to be in the sakala state.
2168.nuance: கலாதி and இராகாதி are the impure tattvas of kala, vidya, raga and the rest, which maya produces to rouse the soul. சகலம் is the embodied state between kevala and suddha.

2169.reading: Like a blind man whose eyes are open, who sees only the step ahead and goes feeling with a stick, the soul in its three states strives by its deeds.
2169.nuance: The image makes the embodied soul partly sighted: instruments let it see the next step only. சொல்லும் விழிபெற (to gain the eye that is spoken of) may hint at the guru's word as the cure; மூவயின் (three places) is unclear.

2170.reading: As a spider sits at the centre of its web and feeds on the life it catches, so the master sits in the golden house of the five senses and consumes the five beginning with sound.
2170.nuance: அத்தன் usually names the Lord, but the one who enjoys sense objects is in Siddhanta the soul; the verse can be read of either, or of the Lord as the soul's inner ruler.

2171.reading: Beyond the twenty-five tattvas set each in its place there is One who reaches to the summit; calling him the mad one, the great one, the unborn, and longing for him, I was saved by his grace.
2171.nuance: பிச்சன் (the mad one) is a loving epithet of Siva, the wandering beggar. The verse breaks the run of counting with personal devotion: the tattvas are named, but grace saves.

2172.reading: Twenty-four with purusha and its true tattva, twenty-five again with the true purusha and the Supreme, and taking the undivided void as the Supreme: so are counted the twenty-eight tattvas of Vedanta.
2172.nuance: The arithmetic is compressed; the verse seems to build the Vedanta count of twenty-eight from the Samkhya twenty-four and twenty-five by adding purusha, the Supreme and the void (வியோமம்).

2173.reading: Taking up ida and pingala, entering with the gunas, and twisting at the root in the triangle, one may see the feet of the Lord who holds time.
2173.nuance: இடை and பிங்கலை are the left and right channels; மூலம் and முக்கோண் are the root centre and its triangle. ஏலம் is obscure, and காலம் கொண்டான் may be the master of time or the one who holds the breath (கால்).

2174.reading: The ten nadis and the vital airs settle in the running breath, and desire, the fluid that bathes, and the mind that seeks the good all lie within the body.
2174.nuance: இரதம் may be the body's essential fluid, often taken as bindu. The verse places breath, desire and mind together in the body, which the yogic chapters treat as the field of practice.

2175.reading: What is to come comes, what is to perish perishes, what is to go goes and what is to enter enters; Nandi, the guardian, showed this and saw it, and the one with shining ornaments does as he bids.
2175.nuance: The doubled verbs state that things run their course. இலங்கிழையோன் (one with shining ornaments) may be Shakti or the soul; ஏவன செய்யும் (does what is commanded) is open as to who commands whom.

2176.reading: Twenty-three with prakriti, turiya, the time known within, the true void and the higher turiya: so the twenty-eight tattvas are to be counted.
2176.nuance: This is a second reckoning of the twenty-eight of 2172; the added items differ. பத்தொடு பத்துமோர் மூன்றும் (ten and ten and three) with பகுதி gives twenty-four.

2177.reading: If the breath runs in the measure of three hundred and thirty and ten, doubled in its seats, the five malas bow, the breath rises, and in that way the tattvas stand clear.
2177.nuance: The numbers are a breath count whose total is unclear; தளங்கொள் இரட்டியது ஆறு may be the six centres doubled. Only the claim that measured breath subdues the malas is plain.

2178.reading: The countless tattvas, numbered in crores and thousands and hundreds, are contained in the ninety-six, and those, when examined, in the twenty-five.
2178.nuance: The exact figure (நாலொரு கோடியே நாற்பத்தொண்ணாயிரம் மேலுமோர் ஐந்நூறு) cannot be fixed; நாற்பத்தொண் may be forty-one or forty-nine. The point is that the many reduce to the few.

2179.reading: The ninety-six are called common to all; the thirty-six are the tattvas of the Saivas; the twenty-eight are for the Vedantins and Vaishnavas; the twenty-four and twenty-five are for the Mayavadins.
2179.nuance: The verse sets the schools' counts side by side without condemning any; அருஞ்சைவர் (the rare Saivas) marks the Saiva count as the one it values. The twenty-four and twenty-five are usually Samkhya numbers, here given to the Mayavadins.

2180.reading: If the tattvas stay in their own course one may live wise and shining, and the false ones fall away; the tattva that is real is the letter A.
2180.nuance: பொய்த்துவம் plays on தத்துவம்: the false against the real. The letter A (அகாரம்) is traditionally Siva, as the first sound in all letters and in Om.

2181.reading: The thirty-five and one are without knowledge; I sat not knowing myself, the one who knows, until Nandi graciously said 'you are the one who knows', and I came to know that I am the knower.
2181.nuance: ஐஏழும் ஒன்றும் (five sevens and one) are the thirty-six tattvas, inert (அறிவொன்றிலாதன). The verse repeats அறி in every line: the soul is set apart from the tattvas as the knower, and learns it only from the guru's word.

2182.reading: Putting away the five states from waking-of-waking, the five mala-states from waking that they produce, and with them the false thirty-six, keeping to the path, the soul stands as one.
2182.nuance: ஒன்றாகியே நிற்கும் (stands having become one) is read here as union; the verse does not name with what.

2183.reading: The five malas from anava belong to the lowest beings, four to Mal, three to Haran, two to the Isvaras, and anava alone to Sadasiva.
2183.nuance: அவரோனுக்கு is obscure (perhaps the lowest, or a slip for Brahma), and நான்காம் மாற்கு is read as நான்கு ஆம் மாற்கு. The grading makes the gods themselves bound souls of higher rank, as Siddhanta holds.

links.note: Both reach the Vedanta count of twenty-eight from the twenty-four, but add different items to it: 2172 purusha, the Supreme and the void, 2176 turiya, inner time, the void and the higher turiya.
2178 reduces the countless tattvas to ninety-six and twenty-five; 2179 says which school counts which, making ninety-six common and thirty-six the Saiva count.
2170 pictures one who sits in the web of the senses and consumes their objects; 2181 separates the knower from all thirty-six inert tattvas, a knowledge the soul gets only from Nandi.
Both make the letter A stand for what is first: the Kural compares God's place in the world to A among letters, and Tirumular names the real tattva the letter A.
2160 says the five malas bind every soul; 2183 grades them by the rank of beings, from five in the lowest to anava alone in Sadasiva.

2167 assigns the sub-states within waking to bonds: waking-of-waking to the concealing power, waking-dream to Mahamaya, and so on. 2253 lists the same sub-states (சாக்கிர சாக்கிரம் தன்னில் கனவொடு ...) and says the five mala-bonds, concealment first (மறையாதி ஐம்மல பாசமே), produce them, giving the general rule of 2167's table.

2163 says the Lord wakes those sunk in anava through blameless Maya (மாயாள் தன்னாலே எழுப்புமே) without saying how. 2168 names what Maya rouses (மாயை எழுப்பும் கலாதியை): kala, raga and the other tattvas, through which the soul comes into the sakala state.

2169 compares the embodied soul to a blind man who sees only the step ahead and goes with a stick (தடிகொண்டு). 2048 has the blind show the stick to the blind (குருடர்க்குக் கோல்காட்டி) and all fall into the pit. In 2169 the stick is the soul's own limited help; in 2048 it is false guidance by another, so the image marks both partial sight and its danger.

2171 calls the One beyond the tattvas the mad one, the great one, the unborn (பிச்சன் பெரியன் பிறப்பிலி) and is saved by longing for him. 1616 names Siva the unborn (பிறப்பிலி) who eats alms and the mad one (பித்தன்) who cuts off births; the same epithets carry the same claim, that the beggar-god is the one who ends birth.

665 says the airs in ida and pingala (இடையொடு பிங்கலை) stand reversed and their hindrances subside. 2173 takes the same two channels, twists the breath at the root triangle (மூலம் கொண்டு முறுக்கி முக்கோணிலும்) and makes the goal the feet of the Lord of time, carrying the practice of 665 to its object.

A near-repeat: 504 has the same four lines (ஆவன ஆவ அழிவ அழிவன / போவன போவ புகுவ புகுவன ...), differing mainly in the last word (இளங்கிளையோன் for இலங்கிழையோன்). The repetition in chapter 49 and here shows the saying, that what is to come comes and what is to go goes, as one Nandi taught in more than one setting.

2175 says what is to come comes and what is to go goes (போவன போவ புகுவ புகுவன). Kural 376 says what is not yours will not stay though guarded, and what is yours will not leave though thrown away (சொரியினும் போகா தம). Both teach that things run their appointed course; 2175 adds that Nandi showed it.

2179 calls the ninety-six tattvas common to all (பொது என்பர்) and lists each school's own count. Arunagiri asks for the common ground (பொதுவை) that holds all the ninety-six tattvas yet stands free of them, which the six sects (அறுவரும்) quarrel over in anger. Both use பொது for what lies under the schools' counts; Arunagiri makes it the truth itself.

A near-repeat: 2323 has the same four lines with small variants (அறிகின்றிலாதன for அறிவொன்றிலாதன, அருள்செய்தான் for அருள்செய்தார்). Both say the thirty-six tattvas do not know, and the soul learns from Nandi's word 'you are the one who knows' that it is the knower; the verse recurs in the chapter on the stainless state.

source_issues: 2167 line 3: அழுத்தி is obscure, perhaps a misprint for சுழுத்தி.
2178: the number in lines 1 and 2 cannot be fixed (நாற்பத்தொண் may be forty-one or forty-nine).
2183 line 1: அவரோனுக்கு is obscure and may be corrupt.
